newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Market steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Market steady in quiet trade.

text.p: The Singapore oil product swaps market drifted in quiet trade late Monday afternoon as the market looked towards late day physical trading and the markets in the west to open for direction, market sources said.
December gas oil swaps was last quoted $31.50/$31.65 a barrel, up about 10 cents from midday but no trades were done, brokers said.
January was traded this afternoon at $30.45 a barrel, unchanged from midday.
Traders said sentiment is firm on expectations of some new buying interest from players who had earlier sold December arrival barrels into Indonesia.
Indonesia is said to have bought a total of around 3.5 million barrels of gas oil for December arrival.
Fuel oil was quoted higher on firm regional demand with Janaury last quoted at $117.50/$118.50 a tonne, up 50 cents from late Friday prices, brokers said.

Traders said the slightl increase was due to the resumption of Chinese demand ahead of the festive season in February. The Chinese market will be closed for one week in February for the Lunar New Year holidays.

China last bought a fuel oil cargo for arrival in late December at close to $8.00 per tonne premium to spot Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis to south China, up about at least 50 cents from the previous purchase.
Bullish sentiment was also due to a reduction in Middle East exports caused by scheduled maintenance at three refineries.
December naphtha remained unchanged in lacklustre trade at $23.60/$23.90, brokers said.
